Bester Part Three

By: Busisiwe Gumede | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
This update story aims to give the viewer insight into Bester's childhood by speaking to his childhood guardian and his friend. We also catch up on the case by speaking to the father of one of the acc

Unique Selling Point:
Our previous Thabo Bester stories scratched at the surface despite answers to relevant questions at the time about who he was and how he made an escape. But it’s time now to delve deep about Bester’s background and the relationship he had with guards at G4S.
This update story aims to give the viewer insight into the kind of childhood Bester had by speaking to his childhood friend Solomon Mbele, who knew Bester when he was just an infant and they grew up together in a farm where his grandmother was working as a domestic worker. We will also introduce a woman who knew and lived with Bester in his teens. Aunty Shenezz says she met Bester as the son of her friend. Bester and her son went to the same school and he would spend a lot of time together as a result. Until Bester stole her son’s school blazer decorated with sports achievements and used it to con mothers in Hyde Park. And lastly we will speak to a former G4S guard who says Bester was living his best life inside prison.


Summary:
CASE STUDY BREAKDOWN
Moroi Maphou - Former G4S guard
● He says a standard procedure was not followed at the time of the fire.
● Inmate X correctly told us that the body was moved and the cell cleaned soon after the fire happened. Maphou says that under normal circumstances, if the cell burned, it would take more than a day for authorities to clean the cell. But he began to worry when Bester’s cell was cleaned immediately after.
● He says, it was actually the Inmate Information Services that was supposed to handle the cleanup then other authorities brought in. the IIS regulates all inmate admissions and services. They also generate prisoner profiles. The IIS would have been the one to contact the family regarding the death of a prisoner. ISS, according to the former G4S guard, was brought in at a later stage.
● He says when Thabo Bester, arrived he was deemed high-risk and that meant that he was to be treated with caution. But that didn’t last long. He became a “star inmate”, he

says, when wardens realised how much money he had. Guards under normal circumstances were supposed to monitor his moves but that was not the case. He says Bester got his way with management. He says money bought Betser privileges in prison. He “owned” most of the guards who came to work at different times of the day”.
Solomon Mbele - Childhood friend
As a child, Solomon Mbele came with his family to johannesburg. His grandmother and Bester’s grandmother all worked together in a farm in ekeinhof. He says Bester’s grandmother loved him dearly and she spoilt him rotten. Their grandmothers would work during the day and Solomon, who was seven at the time, was left to take care of Beter. They would play together and life was great. Solomon connect the dots for us:
● To answer why Bester was raised by his grandmother Johanna Magagula
● Why Bester left that farm and moved somewhere else in Joburg
● How he later linked up with Bester in his teens and he told him that he was a big
musician in joburg
● Years later he was worried when he realised that his childhood friend had turned into the
facebook rapist.
Aunty Shenezz - Bester’s Childhood Guardian
Shenezz says she fell in love with Bester when she became close with his mother.
At the time , he was just 11 years old and attended school with his son at the Danie Theron Primary School in Kibler Park.
He became a regular visitor in her home, chilling with his son and they also played rugby.
She says Bester was very good at rugby but was unable to make qualifiers because he didnt have a birth certificate.
As they spent more time together they realised that Bester had a stealing problem. He would steal money from them. They eventually had to monitor his school bag every time he would visit. They also realised that at 13 years old, he had a lot of business cards in his bag. This only clicked later in life that it was because he was coning people.
She lost contact with him in grade seven. Someone called her and said they spotted Bester walking the streets of Hyde Park with her son's jacket on. He used the blazer decorated with multiple sports achievements to con women, making them believe he had been selected for a school rugby tour and needed money for transport and food.

They, after a few years, received a call from Bussas, the juvenile prison, saying they should come and fetch her son's blazer.
This will link nicely with a previously recorded & unused interview we did with Andre Snyman who was called to assist a group of Hyde Park moms who were conned by Thabo Bester. Bester was apprehended by the school’s officials (including Snyman) and was grilled by them. He promised not to do it again. But after a few days he was back to his old ways. That’s when he was nabbed by the police that Aunty Shennez talks about.

Extra Budget Items:
Transport - Travelling to bloemfontein. Total amount is R2800 - R800 x R3,50.

VO – Fond memories... of her son's childhood friend. A boy who'd later become one of the country’s most infamous criminals.
PARENT OF BESTER'S CHILDHOOD FRIEND
We took him on as if it's one of my sons as well. - 03:02
VO – His name was Thabo Bester, and though unimaginable back then, he’d gain notoriety as the man behind a diabolical prison break; his freedom allegedly made possible through a suspicious fire... corrupt officials… and a DEAD BODY.
BREATHER – dip to black and then go to viz from previous episodes – upsound arrest of Bester and Nandipha in Tanzania
VO – Since their arrest in Tanzania three months ago, Bester and his alleged accomplice, Dr Nandipha Magudumana, have been joined in the dock by ten more suspects.
BREATHER – courtroom natsound
O – It’s alleged one of them helped Dr Magudumana obtain the body used as a decoy in the brazen escape. The remains were identified as those of a man called Katlego Bereng.
Another suspect, Dr Magudumana’s father, is believed to have hired the car used to transport the body to Mangaung Prison. Investigators say the vehicle was driven by yet another of the suspects, a supervisor at G4S - the company that owns the prison.
Seven further suspects, mostly prison employees, have been charged with violating the body and aiding the escape... some, by disabling cameras and unlocking gates though which Bester would simply stroll to freedom...


BREATHER – suspenseful music over shots of the prison entrance, wide shots, etc
MOROI MPHOU – FORMER G4S GUARD
42:39 - The people in the box. I call them sardines. They are just babies shame. I’m sorry to say. They are just babies. There are giants behind this thing.
VO Moroi Mphou is a former Magaung prison guard. He says for such a sophisticated plot to succeed, senior staff like those, now facing charges of facilitating payments, had to be involved.
MOROI MPHOU – FORMER G4S GUARD
It’s all about money. … - 09:15
VO – And, despite serving a life sentence for rape and murder, Thabo Bester had deep pockets.
MOROI MPHOU – FORMER G4S GUARD

CLAIRE 39:46 do you think Thabi Bester was an influential prisoner in the facility?

39:46 Remember if you control the head of the snake, it’ll never bite you.

40:07 Thabo Bester - according to an informant of mine - had hard cash.


VO – But Bester also had something money couldn’t buy: he’d mastered the art of persuasion. It was a skill that fuelled his graduation from petty criminal... to con artist... and eventually... murderer.


PAUSE

VO - Now, ahead o f the trial of those accused of enabling his escape, we gain more insight into Bester’s personality… his shrewdness, his cunning.
… And into how he assumed a dominant role in prison... among both inmates and some prison officials.


BREATHER – transition to Claire link
LINK - Former Mangaung Prison guard, Morui Mphou, was a programs supervision officer and says that when Thabo Bester arrived at the facility, prison guards were warned to be careful not to engage him.
BREATHER – upsound a bit of natsound from the cutaways
VO – That’s because it’s easy for an observant, manipulative inmate, like Bester, to spot a guard in financial trouble.
MOROI MPHOU – FORMER G4S GUARD
07:13 - They will just come out of the cell and look at you. On Monday, what is it that you eating. On the 25th when you get your salary, what is your behaviour.
07:46 - ... “What are you smoking?” “No I'm smoking this type of a cigarette.” So they know the level of the cigarette means you have money but if you're smoking this one, they already know that you probably are broke.

VO – Then, the favours... insignificant ones at first... escalating to serious requests... paid for in cash that is smuggled into the facility.
BREATHER
VO – And when it came to manipulation, Bester was head and shoulders above other inmates. A testament to
having had an early start in crime...


BREATHER
PARENT OF BESTER'S CHILDHOOD FRIEND - SHENEEZ
03:12 - ... My son's phone got missing in the house.
03:30 - ... Thabo just left early and he was gone. Came back in the afternoon, had money on him ... I told my son: “I think he sold the phone.”
03:44
??? - and then money got missing in the house. - 05:04
NEW VO: This is Thabo Bester's one-time guardian. We'll call her “Letty” to protect her true identity. VO Her son's school blazer was next to go… adorned with scrolls, it symbolised his academic and sporting excellence.


PARENT OF BESTER'S CHILDHOOD FRIEND
07:14 - ... we got a call from the friend telling us that: “Listen here, I saw Thabo walking on the highway with the blazer of your son.” - 07:33


VO – The older he got, the better Bester became at getting what he wanted.


LINK - Inmates in the country are not allowed to have unsupervised devices like laptops and cellphones behind bars. If that is the case, how is it that a convicted rapist and murderer ran a business from prison?

BREATHER

VO – How it happened remains to be answered but it’s clear from this cell phone footage that - for Bester - being behind bars wasn’t a barrier to privilege.
MOROI MPHOU – FORMER G4S GUARD
12:01 - ... He has a nice tone to him.
12:13 - … CLAIRE - He’s charming? PLEASE SUBTITLE
Definitely. He can make an onion cry.
42:30 - I think he got and became cocky, and said you know what, “I can now leave this prison. I am now running this facility. Let me go out”.

VO – After his escape, Bester returned to live... and shop... in Hyde Park, an upmarket Johannesburg suburb once the teenage Bester’s happy hunting ground.
Andre Snyman, founder of the E Blockwatch crime prevention app, met the young Bester 17 years ago.
ANDRE SNYMAN – ANTI-CRIME ACTIVIST
04:48 – He was a lovely guy, he was a friendly guy.
VO: And, judging by his blazer, he was clever and good at sport - or was he?
01:07 – ... he was dressed in a uniform and he had all the scrolls and he looked like a schoolboy.


VO – The mystery of the missing blazer resolved.
ANDRE SNYMAN – ANTI-CRIME ACTIVIST
01:21 - ... He was scamming the mothers trying to get money just like the normal kind of thing, and the mothers would dish out the money.

PARENT OF BESTER'S CHILDHOOD FRIEND
13:50 - I was very angry with him. I was sad. I couldn't believe what this child did.
VO – Bester was eventually arrested near the high school he claimed to be attending.
ANDRE SNYMAN – EBLOCKWATCH
04:35 – ... He had the confidence of a head boy. He had a uniform with all the scrolls so it was very easy to be taken in by this guy.
VO – Snyman didn’t hear of Bester again until 5 years later.. 2011… the year he was convicted of robbing and raping women he met on Facebook.
The following year, he was found guilty of killing Nomfundo Tyhlo - a young woman he’d met in the same way.
PAUSE

Now, close to a decade after being sentenced, a handwritten letter he sent from prison to the family that had taken him in as a young boy provides a rare glimpse into Thabo Bester’s mind..


SOUND UP - CLAIRE AND SHANEEZ READING BESTERS LETTER.

CLIP 0079 - 00:05 CLAIRE: “Thabo says, I was sitting in a jail cell facing a possible life sentence. It was a time of terrible fear, darkness and despair”

CLIP 0077 02:41 CLAIRE : “Bester writes, my grandmother shaped me in many ways. She didn't have education, but she had superb values, and your mother sent us to church. We grew up in that environment. To respect women. So all the things that people say I have done is not true…wow”


BREATHER – dip to black, then transition creatively to Claire link
LINK - Thabo Bester’s daring escape from Mangaung prison raises many questions about the relationship between inmates and guards at the facility. All indications are that Bester planned his bid for freedom with the help of senior prison officials. He must have known that the guards felt that they were underpaid, and he used that information to orchestrate his escape.
BREATHER

MOROI MPHOU – FORMER G4S GUARD
All the directors that were there that day, did not go according to policy.
Why are they not being arrested? Why are they being not being suspended?
VO – The investigation into one of the country’s most sensational and sinister crimes continues as more and more suspects face trial in August. But, for one heartbroken woman, the idea that Bester was its mastermind is a bitter pill.
CLAIRE – 25:43... Did Thabo Bester con you?
26:11 - ... I don't know if he really conned me at that time because the way he used to talk things and tell me. I did not think that he is a criminal. - 26:23


VO – Perhaps, though, a clue lies in the very letter he wrote to her in 2015. Amidst the heartwarming memories of years past, are hints at the true nature of Thabo Bester.

03:45 -My body hurts ... My diabetes is type 2.
03:55 So - ... I need to get meals. that we don't get from the prison.
04:05 … the food in prison has salt and sugar… I need money to get food from the shop.

VO – After his escape, Bester returned to live... and shop... in Hyde Park, an upmarket Johannesburg suburb once the teenage Bester’s happy hunting ground. Andre Snyman, founder of the E Blockwatch crime prevention app, met the young Bester 17 years ago. ANDRE SNYMAN – ANTI-CRIME ACTIVIST 04:48 – He was a lovely guy, he was a friendly guy. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): This update story aims to give the viewer insight into Bester's childhood by speaking to his childhood guardian and his friend. We also catch up on the case by speaking to the father of one of the acc
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Our previous Thabo Bester stories scratched at the surface despite answers to relevant questions at the time about who he was and how he made an escape. But it’s time now to delve deep about Bester’s background and the relationship he had with guards at G4S. This update story aims to give the viewer insight into the kind of childhood Bester had by speaking to his childhood friend Solomon Mbele, who knew Bester when he was just an infant and they grew up together in a farm where his grandmother was working as a domestic worker. We will also introduce a woman who knew and lived with Bester in his teens. Aunty Shenezz says she met Bester as the son of her friend. Bester and her son went to the same school and he would spend a lot of time together as a result. Until Bester stole her son’s school blazer decorated with sports achievements and used it to con mothers in Hyde Park. And lastly we will speak to a former G4S guard who says Bester was living his best life inside prison.
metadata.Summary: CASE STUDY BREAKDOWN Moroi Maphou - Former G4S guard ● He says a standard procedure was not followed at the time of the fire. ● Inmate X correctly told us that the body was moved and the cell cleaned soon after the fire happened. Maphou says that under normal circumstances, if the cell burned, it would take more than a day for authorities to clean the cell. But he began to worry when Bester’s cell was cleaned immediately after. ● He says, it was actually the Inmate Information Services that was supposed to handle the cleanup then other authorities brought in. the IIS regulates all inmate admissions and services. They also generate prisoner profiles. The IIS would have been the one to contact the family regarding the death of a prisoner. ISS, according to the former G4S guard, was brought in at a later stage. ● He says when Thabo Bester, arrived he was deemed high-risk and that meant that he was to be treated with caution. But that didn’t last long. He became a “star inmate”, he says, when wardens realised how much money he had. Guards under normal circumstances were supposed to monitor his moves but that was not the case. He says Bester got his way with management. He says money bought Betser privileges in prison. He “owned” most of the guards who came to work at different times of the day”. Solomon Mbele - Childhood friend As a child, Solomon Mbele came with his family to johannesburg. His grandmother and Bester’s grandmother all worked together in a farm in ekeinhof. He says Bester’s grandmother loved him dearly and she spoilt him rotten. Their grandmothers would work during the day and Solomon, who was seven at the time, was left to take care of Beter. They would play together and life was great. Solomon connect the dots for us: ● To answer why Bester was raised by his grandmother Johanna Magagula ● Why Bester left that farm and moved somewhere else in Joburg ● How he later linked up with Bester in his teens and he told him that he was a big musician in joburg ● Years later he was worried when he realised that his childhood friend had turned into the facebook rapist. Aunty Shenezz - Bester’s Childhood Guardian Shenezz says she fell in love with Bester when she became close with his mother. At the time , he was just 11 years old and attended school with his son at the Danie Theron Primary School in Kibler Park. He became a regular visitor in her home, chilling with his son and they also played rugby. She says Bester was very good at rugby but was unable to make qualifiers because he didnt have a birth certificate. As they spent more time together they realised that Bester had a stealing problem. He would steal money from them. They eventually had to monitor his school bag every time he would visit. They also realised that at 13 years old, he had a lot of business cards in his bag. This only clicked later in life that it was because he was coning people. She lost contact with him in grade seven. Someone called her and said they spotted Bester walking the streets of Hyde Park with her son's jacket on. He used the blazer decorated with multiple sports achievements to con women, making them believe he had been selected for a school rugby tour and needed money for transport and food. They, after a few years, received a call from Bussas, the juvenile prison, saying they should come and fetch her son's blazer. This will link nicely with a previously recorded & unused interview we did with Andre Snyman who was called to assist a group of Hyde Park moms who were conned by Thabo Bester. Bester was apprehended by the school’s officials (including Snyman) and was grilled by them. He promised not to do it again. But after a few days he was back to his old ways. That’s when he was nabbed by the police that Aunty Shennez talks about.
